rationale:
Evidence: iteration 5 (kp 2.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.0, search_right, sensors at x = -0.04, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.04 with y = 0.05, sensor_size 0.012) is the best raced design at 75.779. Iteration 10 reproduced it exactly, so the design is confirmed as the base. Every single-field change tested since then has lost score: kp 1.6 gave 51.18, sensor_size 0.016 gave 60.12, kd 0.2 gave 69.03, and base_speed 1.1 gave 51.33. Every run ends with one line-loss event and max_error of about 0.062 to 0.067 m, above the 0.06 m limit, with low oscillation, so the failure is a slow drift to one edge.

Change: none. I reproduce the iteration 5 design unchanged. This is the final iteration, so no later race can use what this race shows. An untested lever such as the wider sensor span (H14, outer sensors at x = plus or minus 0.05 m) could raise or lower the score, and it cannot be checked by a review run, because only the race itself reveals it. Since the final unseen-track race is scored, I keep the design that has the best measured result across development tracks.

Expected result: about 75.8 on the development tracks, with progress near oval 0.29, s-bend 0.15 and slalom 0.11, and one line-loss event per run. Hypotheses to check on the race: (1) if the score matches 75.8, the run is deterministic and the design is reproduced; (2) if the score differs, the run is not deterministic, and that should be noted before any future change. Measurements wanted: progress, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track, and whether the line-loss point moves along the course.
